newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hashimoto to begin ASEAN tour despite Lima crisis.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto to begin ASEAN tour despite Lima crisis.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto will leave on Tuesday for an eight-day tour of Southeast Asia despite the Peru hostage situation.

The Japanese leader undertakes the mission in an air of pessimism that the remaining 74 hostages held by left-wing Peruvian guerrillas in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima will be released soon.

Hashimoto's trip to five Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) members -- Brunei, Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam and Singapore -- is aimed at bolstering Japan's ties with the region and mustering support for Japanese foreign policy initiatives.
"The ASEAN countries, positioned as the core of the Asia-Pacific region, have joined hands with Japan in the past," Hashimoto said on Saturday. "I would like to deepen that relationship."
In a key policy speech in Singapore on January 14, the Japanese premier will try to cast off Japan's meek image on the world stage.
He is expected to spell his "Hashimoto doctrine", an outline of Japan's policies regarding the Asia-Pacific region.
Hashimoto's Asia-Pacific strategy is expected to be underpinned by increasing economic cooperation with ASEAN countries and aimed at containing China's growing influence in the region.

China and Japan last year waged a war of words over the Senkaku Islands, called the Diaoyu Islands by Beijing. Located in the East China Sea, the area around the islands is thought to contain huge oil and gas reserves.
Hashimoto said on Saturday that during his visit he will also propose regular summit-level consultations between Japan and the seven ASEAN nations, which also include the Philippines and Thailand.

The proposal comes as ASEAN heads of government plan for a ministerial meeting on February 13-14 with the European Union and Japan against a background of increasing European interest in exchanges with Southeast Asia.
Hashimoto is also likely to drum up backing among ASEAN leaders for Japan's bid for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council.
